views.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. SINGLE landscape interior photograph. Input image1 is EDIT TARGET, the TV-wall view from Living Room01. Input image2 is the close-up REFERENCE OF USER'S ACTUAL SHELF ORNAMENTS; restore these exactly instead of generic shelf props in edit target. Input image3 is the original full-room geometry/furniture reference IMG_8641, not a separate panel.
Keep image1 camera framing, perspective, wall-mounted TV and room layout.
Living Room 02 - Collected, Not Matching.
User feedback: floating walnut cabinet is too modern, repeated beige Persian rugs/generic pottery make every room alike. They want an OLDER, INDIVIDUAL room using their REAL ornaments. Treat their collection as important, not clutter.
LOCK ARCHITECTURE AND ROOM: original pale grey/off-white wall, ceiling and white panelling colours, cornice, floorboards, black steel reception doors, kitchen/dining/garden geometry. No repainting, wood slat cladding, new joinery, fireplace or structural redesign. Keep wall-mounted TV at same low height and SAME screen size. Keep current straight taupe sofa size/location/colour, three existing muted rust/olive/flax cushions, original small marble side table with brass/linen lamp at RECEPTION END of sofa, retained monstera, grey raised dog bed at KITCHEN END of sofa. Preserve working route from black steel doors to kitchen.
CHANGE BENEATH TV: remove floating modern walnut cabinet completely. On floor below TV put a LOW ANTIQUE-STYLE OAK COFFER/BLANKET CHEST, around130-140cm W,35-40cm D,45-48cm H, visibly freestanding on small worn feet/base with real floor beneath edges, aged dark honey/oak patina, simple two-panel front, a little irregular worn grain, restrained old iron hinges/lock plate. Distinct old furniture with character, NOT an enormous medieval chest, distressed-white farmhouse piece, modern fluted/slatted sideboard, floating unit or media cabinet. Top mostly clear, at most one small of user's objects if needed. TV remains MOUNTED, not standing on chest. No invented wall repaint or socket removal; wiring provision conceptual.
RUG: COMPLETELY DIFFERENT FROM PREVIOUS FLORAL PERSIAN rugs. An aged flatwoven KILIM-STYLE rug with muted brick/terracotta, ochre/flax, subdued slate/indigo blue and small olive accents. Large-scale stepped diamond/lozenge geometry with irregular woven edges and old flatweave wool texture, NOT tiny repeated floral motifs, beige distressed medallions or modern abstract graphic canvas. Earthy softened dyes but clearly more character and colour, NOT saturated primary red. Pattern scale feels traditional handwoven. Large rug anchors sofa/table, front sofa feet on it, oak margins before steel doors and kitchen; main TV-side walk route clear. No tassels across circulation.
TABLE: replace generic modern oval walnut coffee table with a small vintage-style dark-stained wooden TRAY-TOP coffee table with slender TURNED legs and low stretchers, around70-75x40-45cm, rectangular with softly rounded corners, modest height. Not big bulky trunk or another matching oak chest. Keep top almost empty, one remote or existing small dish only.
SOFA WALL: RESTORE USER'S ACTUAL LARGE ROUND CLOCK from original photo, dark rim and cream face, above sofa within original panelling. Remove the newly invented landscape painting. Do not add another generic painting. Clock is a useful personal existing piece, not new modern art.
SHELF AND COLLECTED OBJECTS: retain original black leaning ladder frame and wood shelves, exact 5 shelves, width and height. Input close-up image is the CRITICAL SOURCE for actual ornaments; reproduce shapes/materials as faithfully as image generation allows, do not substitute generic pottery, new photo frames, beige vases or fake plants. KEEP these identifiable existing pieces:
Top shelf: dark seated figure in middle with two small dark cylindrical holders beside it, as photo.
Second shelf: pair of copper/terracotta-coloured cylindrical pots at one side, little ornate tower-shaped lidded ornament, and the existing brown decorative scene plate on a small stand at other side.
Middle shelf: the rich RED GLASS circular piece/bowl, the dark patterned spherical ornament, and the SILVER-TONED figurine; retain identity and colour.
Next shelf: the small low pale bird/duck, the cream camel-like animal figure and the small upright carved brown figure, kept as the user's actual personal miniatures.
Bottom shelf: user's real mixed book group.
Keep small gaps, let objects read in groups, but DO NOT remove the original collection in the name of minimalism. It is okay that these shelves have several meaningful ornaments; avoid adding NEW ornaments. Remove generic trailing shelf/cabinet plants from previous design so real objects can show. Do not recolour everything beige.
HAT: keep same existing deep RED VIETNAMESE HAT above ladder shelf as in previous proposal, one hat only. Warm red hat/glass piece relate to muted brick rug, not matching decorative red purchases. Hat doesn't move to next TV.
Retain MONSTERA as principal floor plant in original TV-wall/kitchen-side location, no extra tropical forest. No additional generic props or new books to create atmosphere. Background kitchen and reception not redesigned; remove people/temporary staging clutter only.
Photorealistic existing home with mixed older furniture, collected objects and warm natural daylight, truthful unchanged paint, not a showroom or matched furniture suite. No cartoon, glossy CGI, people, text labels, arrows, watermarks or collage.

Current owned ornaments and clock are restored using photo references. All older files retained. Rendered identities/materials and dimensions are approximations, not proof of authenticity or fit. Final outputs copied without post-processing.
